levi

Source: R/levi.R
levi.Rd

This is the Levi script mode. It allows you to create the integration of networks and gene expression levels as batch processing

levi(
  expressionInput,
  fileTypeInput,
  networkCoordinatesInput,
  networkInteractionsInput = NA,
  geneSymbolInput,
  readExpColumn,
  contrastValueInput = 50,
  zoomValueInput = 50,
  resolutionValueInput = 50,
  smoothValueInput = 50,
  expressionLog = FALSE,
  contourLevi = FALSE,
  setcolor = "default",
  plot3d = FALSE,
  n_perm = 0,
  sig_level = 0.05,
  perm_side = c("both", "over", "under"),
  signal_mode = c("ratio", "logfc", "zscore"),
  logfc_k = 1,
  p_adjust_method = "BY",
  region_threshold = 0.1,
  region_min_cells = 3L,
  inference_unit = c("region", "cell"),
  perm_strata = NULL,
  edge_weighting = c("midpoint", "degree", "none"),
  .parsed_network = NULL,
  .draw = TRUE
)

Arguments

expressionInput

File path to gene expression data (tab-delimited), OR a data.frame / matrix directly. When passing a data.frame, it must contain a gene identifier column and at least one expression column. Objects from leviFromDESeq2(), leviFromEdgeR(), leviFromLimma(), and leviFromSeurat() are accepted directly.

fileTypeInput

Format of the biological network, given as one of "dat" (Medusa), "dyn" (RedeR), "net" (Pajek) or "stg" (STRING/STITCH). This is the format code, not a file name: the network itself is passed in networkCoordinatesInput.

networkCoordinatesInput

File path to the biological network carrying the node coordinates, OR a data.frame with them directly (as returned in $nodes by leviFromSTRING()). The format must match fileTypeInput.

networkInteractionsInput

Parameter available only to STRING/STITCH data format. It allows the user to load the interaction data file of the network.

geneSymbolInput

Column name from gene expression data containing the identifier (gene Symbol, Entrez ID, EMSEMBL, etc).

readExpColumn

Variable from readExpColumn function containing the comparisons of the experiments

contrastValueInput

Numeric value controlling how tightly the landscape hugs the network. The landscape is built by normalised convolution, and this parameter sets the occupancy threshold below which a grid cell is considered background and returned as NA: higher values give a tighter silhouette. The variable range is 0 to 100. The default value is 50.

zoomValueInput

Numeric value for image zoom, from 0 (widest frame) to 100 (tightest). The grid always leaves enough margin around the network for the smoothed silhouette to fit, whatever the smoothing and contrast; the zoom adds up to 20% of the network extent on top of that margin. The default value is 50.

resolutionValueInput

Numeric value for image resolution. The variable range is 0 to 100. The default value is 50.

smoothValueInput

Numeric value for image smoothness. Sets the width (\(\sigma\)) of the Gaussian kernel used by the normalised convolution, scaled relative to resolutionValueInput so that changing the resolution does not change the apparent smoothing. Unlike in levi < 2.0.0, this parameter no longer affects the value scale, only the level of detail. The variable range is 0 to 100. The default is 50.

expressionLog

Logical. In ratio mode, TRUE back-transforms log2 expression with 2^x before calculation. Ignored in logfc and zscore modes, which use log-scale columns directly. Default FALSE.

contourLevi

Logical variable to allow contour lines. The default is FALSE.

setcolor

Select the color palette to build the heatmat. There is two options the **Multicolor** has 20 color levels combined. The **Two colors** has two types of color and the options available are: *purple_pink*, *green_blue*, *blue_yellow*, *pink_green*, *orange_purple*, *green_marine*.

plot3d

Logical. When TRUE, an interactive 3D surface plot is additionally generated using plotly. Requires the plotly package. Default is FALSE.

n_perm

Integer. Number of node-label permutations, default 0. Measured node expression pairs are shuffled together; missing positions stay fixed and edge signals are recalculated. Tests spatial association conditional on the chosen network/layout, not differential expression between replicates. Raw Monte Carlo p-values are (count + 1)/(n_perm + 1). A larger number improves resolution but does not establish biological validity.

sig_level

Numeric (0-1). Significance threshold for the contour overlay. A contour is drawn wherever the p-value equals sig_level. Default is 0.05.

perm_side

Character. Which direction to test when n_perm > 0. Options:

"both"

(default) dashed contour for over-expression + dotted for under-expression.

"over"

Only the dashed contour.

"under"

Only the dotted contour.

result$pvalues is a list with $over and $under matrices when inference_unit = "cell", or NULL when n_perm = 0 or in regional mode, where perm_side selects which significant regions are outlined.

signal_mode

Character. How raw expression values are converted to the landscape score in \([0,1]\). Choose based on your data type:

"ratio"

(default) \(Test / (Test + Control)\), without min-max normalisation; equal nonzero values map to 0.5. Best for linear-scale data: raw counts, TPM, FPKM, linear proteomics LFQ. Also correct when expressionLog = TRUE is used to back-transform log2 microarray intensities into linear scale.

"logfc"

Sigmoid transformation: \(1 / (1 + e^{-k \cdot \text{logFC}})\) where \(k\) = logfc_k and \(\text{logFC} = Test - Control\) for two log-scale columns, or the supplied logFC in single-column mode. Score 0.5 = no change; > 0.5 = up-regulated; < 0.5 = down-regulated. Best for: RMA microarray, VST/rlog from DESeq2, log2 proteomics, scRNA-seq avg_log2FC (single-column mode with readExpColumn("logFC-logFC")).

"zscore"

Z-scores the logFC distribution then maps to \([0,1]\) via pnorm(). Score 0.5 = mean logFC of measured nodes and derived edge support points; tails approach 0/1. This is relative within each comparison and uses mean/SD, not a robust estimator. It does not encode an absolute no-change baseline.

logfc_k

Numeric. Steepness of the sigmoid in signal_mode = "logfc". Larger values make the transition from 0 to 1 sharper (more contrast between up/down). Default is 1. Typical range: 0.5-3. Use k = 0.5 for datasets with large logFC values (e.g., scRNA-seq fold-changes often range +/-5) and k = 2 for tight fold-changes (e.g., +/-1 in microarray).

p_adjust_method

Multiple-testing correction used only when inference_unit = "cell", applied jointly to both directional families over occupied grid cells in each comparison. Default "BY" accommodates arbitrary dependence; "BH", "holm", "none" and other methods accepted by stats::p.adjust are available. Contours and pvalues use these adjusted values; raw_pvalues is unadjusted.

region_threshold

Positive deviation from the neutral score 0.5 used to define a regional cell. The default 0.1 identifies cells >= 0.6 or <= 0.4. This parameter describes regions and does not assign statistical significance.

region_min_cells

Minimum number of eight-connected grid cells retained as a region. Default is 3.

inference_unit

Either "region" (default) or "cell" (legacy). With "region" and n_perm > 0, regions are redetected in every node-label permutation and the observed mass of each region is compared with the maximum mass across all regions and both directions. Results are in regions$summary$PSpatial and $Significant; regions$null_max_mass stores the null maxima. This controls the search under the global exchangeable spatial null, conditional on network/layout. It does not establish significance of individual cells or genes, precise boundaries, or differences between biological replicates. pvalues and raw_pvalues are NULL in regional mode; the 2D plot labels areas rather than named gene peaks and white boundaries mark regions passing sig_level. The 3D plot shows the descriptive surface without regional boundaries.

"cell" tests every occupied grid cell separately and adjusts the two directional families jointly with p_adjust_method. Cells are strongly correlated, so that adjustment is very conservative; the mode is kept for the graphical interface and for comparison with earlier versions. See vignette("levi_inference") for which null answers which question.

perm_strata

Optional vector defining exchangeability strata for the node-label permutation. A named vector is matched to network gene identifiers; an unnamed vector must follow network-node order. Signals are shuffled only among measured nodes in the same stratum. Useful for bins of mean expression, detection rate or network degree. Default `NULL` permutes all measured nodes.

edge_weighting

Character. How the edge midpoints enter the landscape. "midpoint" (default, the historical behaviour) gives every node and every edge midpoint the same weight, so a hub of degree \(d\) surrounds itself with \(d\) support points and dominates its neighbourhood. "degree" weights the midpoint of edge \((i, j)\) by \((1/d_i + 1/d_j)/2\), so the midpoints around any node add up to one whatever its degree. "none" drops the midpoints and smooths the node values alone. All three keep the same coordinates, silhouette logic and permutation nulls; the choice is recorded in metadata$edge_weighting and reused by the sample-label tests.

.parsed_network, .draw

Internal controls used to reuse a parsed network and suppress repeated drawing in resampling workflows.

Value

Invisibly returns a list (or a list of such lists, one per comparison, when readExpColumn carries more than one) containing:

comparison

Name of the comparison (e.g. "Tumor-Normal").

landscape

data.frame with the plotted surface in long format (Var1, Var2, z). Cells outside the network silhouette are NA, not 0. Required by leviDiff.

scores

data.frame with one row per network node (Gene, X, Y, LandscapeScore, Rank), ordered from the highest score to the lowest.

peaks

data.frame with the automatically detected peaks and valleys (Type, NearestGene, MatrixRow, MatrixCol, Score).

pvalues

list with the $over and $under permutation p-value matrices in cell mode, or NULL when n_perm = 0 or inference_unit = "region".

raw_pvalues

Unadjusted directional permutation p-values, or NULL.

regions

List with summary (one row per eight-connected area) and cells (member grid cells). In regional inference mode, the summary also contains PSpatial and Significant; null_max_mass and inference record the null and method. Otherwise regions are descriptive.

metadata

Signal meaning, parameters, network, coordinates, missing genes, RNG state before calculation and software versions. Call set.seed() before levi() for reproducibility.

plot

the ggplot object, also drawn on the active device.

plot3d

the plotly surface when plot3d = TRUE, otherwise NULL. Like plot, it is also shown when produced. To save it from a chosen viewpoint, set the camera and write the file:


    p <- plotly::layout(result$plot3d, scene = list(camera = list(
             eye = list(x = 1.6, y = -1.6, z = 0.9))))
    htmlwidgets::saveWidget(p, "surface.html")  # interactive, keeps the view
    leviSave3D(p, "surface.png")                # static; needs kaleido

eye is the camera position relative to the centre of the surface; larger values move it away. Interactively, rotate the surface and use the camera icon of the plotly toolbar to save the current view as PNG.

Details

Integrates the biological network and gene expression levels (or other type of data). In single-column ratio mode, the score is abundance/(abundance + 1), with no control comparison. Missing measurements and undefined ratios are assigned 0.5. Surface, scores, peaks and tests use the same Gaussian-smoothed signal. A gene's smoothed score also reflects its neighbours, so a locally unchanged gene can receive a non-neutral score.

Every edge contributes a support point at its midpoint, carrying the mean of its two endpoints. With the default edge_weighting = "midpoint" a hub with many edges places many support points around itself and dominates the local average: the landscape is implicitly weighted by degree. The node-label permutation test keeps the network fixed, so this weighting is part of its null and does not bias the inference, but it does shape what the eye reads on the figure. edge_weighting = "degree" removes that emphasis while keeping the edges as carriers of neighbourhood signal; "none" smooths the nodes alone.

Examples

template_network <- file.path(system.file(package="levi"),"extdata",
   "medusa.dat", fsep = .Platform$file.sep)

template_expression <- file.path(system.file(package="levi"),
   "extdata","expression.dat", fsep = .Platform$file.sep)

multicolor <- levi(networkCoordinatesInput = template_network,
   expressionInput = template_expression, fileTypeInput = "dat",
   geneSymbolInput = "ID",
   readExpColumn=readExpColumn("TumorCurrentSmoker-NormalNeverSmoker"),
   contrastValueInput = 50, resolutionValueInput  = 50, zoomValueInput = 50,
   smoothValueInput = 50, expressionLog = FALSE, contourLevi = TRUE)
#> There are 1 nodes without expression value, see log in path: /tmp/RtmpNc6BNs/TumorCurrentSmoker-NormalNeverSmoker/levi.log


twocolors <- levi(networkCoordinatesInput = template_network,
   expressionInput = template_expression, fileTypeInput = "dat",
   geneSymbolInput = "ID",
   readExpColumn = readExpColumn("TumorCurrentSmoker-NormalNeverSmoker"),
   setcolor = "pink_green", contourLevi = FALSE)
#> There are 1 nodes without expression value, see log in path: /tmp/RtmpNc6BNs/TumorCurrentSmoker-NormalNeverSmoker/levi.log
